newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ delays May jobless data amid computer problems.
newsitem.headline: NZ delays May jobless data amid computer problems.

text.p: New Zealand's employment minister Peter McCardle said on Wednesday that continuing computer difficulties meant the issue of May unemployment figures due on Thursday had been postponed until further notice.

"The figures were due to be released tomorrow morning, however, I am not prepared to release any data until I am confident the statistics are accurate," he said in a statement, adding they were unlikely to be available before June 26.
That date is when the coalition government is due to release its maiden budget.
McCardle said work was continuing on the computer-generated part of the monthly statistics cycle.

"Given the general interest in these unemployment statistics I am not happy with the delay in their release, however, equally I have conveyed to my department that I expect all figures to be an accurate total of the numbers registered as unemployed," he added.
Last month the minister said a computer error caused April data to be overstated by 6,100 people and incorrectly showed a rise when in fact the roll had fallen between March and April.
Corrected regional statistics for April had also been due to be released alongside the May data on Thursday.
